Cautiously hawkish policy message (25 bp hike to 5.25–5.50% and ongoing QT) remains intact. Beige Book references point to modest overall expansion with consumer spending holding up in services/tourism and continued job gains in health care, transportation, and hospitality. However, wages and turnover are returning toward pre‑pandemic norms, indicating easing labor‑market tightness, while consumer prices remain elevated. This aligns with the FOMC’s vigilance on inflation.

The July 2023 SLOOS and Beige Book together indicate broad-based tightening in credit—across CRE (construction, land development, nonfarm nonresidential, multifamily), residential real estate (GSE-eligible, jumbo, government, QM and non-QM), HELOCs, credit cards, and auto loans—with tighter terms and weaker subprime demand. These credit headwinds, particularly for banks with meaningful CRE exposure, suggest a more persistent drag on growth than a pure macro read would imply.

Netting resilient but normalizing labor conditions against tighter credit and still-elevated prices, the overall tone shifts modestly more negative than prior: cautious growth outlook with lingering inflation and stronger credit headwinds.
